items.title: FetchSandbox MCP
items.name: FetchSandbox MCP
items.summary: The MCP that proves your AI's integration fixes work
items.description: Your agent's integration fix passes CI. The data is still wrong. FetchSandbox MCP reproduces the real failure on your code, fixes it, and proves the fix held. A receipt, not a vibe. 70+ API sandboxes. One config block in Cursor or Claude Code.
top_comments:
Raj here, one of the co-founders.

Writing the integration stopped being the hard part. Checking that it actually works is the whole job now, and that's the half your agent can't do.

The gap

Your agent can write a Stripe integration. It can't run one. It writes the code, tells you it's done, and you find out in production whether that was true. FetchSandbox gives the agent already in your editor two things it doesn't have: somewhere real to run integration code, and a way to prove the fix worked.

Why the proof check matters

A customer paid for 5 seats. A retry gave them 10, then 15. An agent fixed it, and after the fix nobody got any seats at all. Tests still passed because the duplicates were gone. Almost any fix makes the error disappear. Far fewer make the data right.

So the gate asserts the exact end state a correct implementation leaves, and refuses to go green when it can't reproduce the bug first.

Setup

One block in your MCP config. No API key, no signup. Works in Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, Windsurf, and Codex. 70+ ready-made sandboxes: Stripe, HubSpot, Clerk, Resend, Twilio and more, free to try.

We hit #3 on our first launch. The ask afterward was exactly this: don't just give me a sandbox, tell me my fix actually worked. This is that.

Has your agent ever confidently fixed something that was still broken?
This has good potential as with QA surface as well. Do you see FetchSandbox being used for e2e QA for dev, test, prod envs.

The 5 seats turning into 15 is the version of this that actually costs money. We hit the same shape at Zeplik, output that parses fine and passes every assertion we wrote, wrong in a way only the end state shows. Green CI on a bad write is worse than a red build because nobody goes back and looks. I'd want to know if the receipt catches partial failures too, 3 of 5 writes landing and the rest silently dropped.

items.title: PaymentKit
items.name: PaymentKit
items.summary: Billing that survives a processor shutdown
items.description: PaymentKit is a multi-processor billing platform for SaaS and e-commerce. It routes payments across processors, vaults tokens independently, and keeps subscriptions billing even if a MID gets shut down. No code to launch, full API when you need it.
top_comments:
Hey everyone, Diego here from the PaymentKit team.

Quick story on where this came from, because it explains most of the product.

PaymentKit didn't start as a startup idea. We built it for ourselves. Our parent company runs a portfolio of subscription brands, and for years we kept hitting the same three problems: billing lived in one tool, payments in another, and revenue data in a third. Every processor change meant a migration. Every decline was money we never saw again. And all of it sat on top of a single processor whose risk team could change our business overnight.

We couldn't find anything that solved all three together, so we built it and ran our own volume through it before selling it to anyone.

What it actually does:

  • Payment orchestration: Connect the processors you already use. Every transaction routes to the one most likely to approve it, and soft declines cascade to the next one automatically instead of turning into lost revenue.

  • Independent vaulting: The part we care most about. Cards, Apple Pay and Google Pay are all vaulted as network tokens under your control, not your processor's. You can add or drop a processor without asking a single customer to re enter anything, and if a MID gets shut down your subscribers never feel it.

  • Subscription billing: Flat, tiered, usage based or hybrid pricing. Hosted checkout and self service portals, live without writing code.

  • Revenue metrics: One dashboard across every processor, so you can compare success rates and fees side by side instead of stitching exports together.

What that actually produces: More than 10% lift in authorization rates on average after merchants switch.

It comes from three things stacked: routing each transaction to the processor most likely to approve it, cascading soft declines instead of eating them, and network tokens that keep cards on file alive longer. One merchant went from 63% to 76%. There's also a risk side that most people only learn the hard way. Visa dropped the excessive VAMP threshold from 2.20% to 1.50% on April 1st this year across the US, Canada, Europe and Asia Pacific, and the ratio is measured per MID, not per company. If all your volume sits in one account, one bad month becomes a company level problem. Running multiple processors means you see the ratio per MID instead of hearing about it from your acquirer after the fact, and you can rebalance volume before any single account gets near the line.

Why I think this community in particular might care: a lot of you are running SaaS or digital products on a single processor, or on a merchant of record that owns your customer data and your tokens. That works right up until it doesn't. We're the layer that makes that decision reversible.

It goes live in under an hour on top of what you already have, and there's a free trial if you want to poke at it.

Would really like to hear from anyone who's been through a processor shutdown, a rolling reserve, or a migration that broke their subscriptions. What did you wish existed at that moment?
I like this as revenue-side redundancy. AI founders obsess over multi-model routing for COGS; surprisingly few apply the same resilience logic to the revenue pipe.

Really like the idea of treating payment processors as replaceable infrastructure instead of something your entire billing stack depends on. Curious how hard it is to migrate an existing saas with active subscriptions into this app?

idea_items.title: 语言 AI 陪练
idea_items.need_line: 学习者苦于口语流利度不足，需要能指出具体音节/发音问题的实时纠错陪练，而不是只给整体分数的跟读工具。
idea_items.status_line: 讨论集中在用开源工具（如 Enjoy App）做逐句跟读评分和音节级纠错，也有人用 Agent 技能（如 ielts-buddy）把口语陪练融入学习计划，共享做法是自选视频/文本转成可练习的分段材料。
idea_items.direction_line: 值得跟踪的方向是让口语陪练支持任意外语视频/文本自动生成带逐句评测和发音定位的练习，并将这类陪练嵌入本地 Agent 工作流。

idea_items.title: 法律 AI 工作流
idea_items.need_line: 律师审一份合同前必须弄清交易模式、背景，客户却以为“甩个文件半小时就能确认”，导致一次审查往往要数天反复沟通。
idea_items.status_line: 普通人习惯直接用网上的模板合同，律师靠微信反复向客户确认背景信息，已有 LexAI 等 LLM 工具把合同审查、起草、对比打包成智能体，但仍未解决背景采集问题。
idea_items.direction_line: 值得跟踪的是让 AI 在审查前主动向用户提问交易结构与商业意图、形成带背景假设的风险清单，而非只对文本做静态审查。

idea_items.title: 供应链分析 Agent
idea_items.need_line: 供应链运营人员补货分析耗时太长，需要能根据历史数据和关键信息自动给出补货建议的智能助手。
idea_items.status_line: 当前做法多是在 GitHub 等开源社区搭建多场景通用决策 Agent（如 DecisionAgent），用信息提取+历史匹配来覆盖供应链等领域，但尚无针对补货分析的专用解决方案。
idea_items.direction_line: 值得跟踪决策 Agent 在供应链补货场景的纵向深化，将历史补货数据、库存阈值和异常波动纳入同一套决策链路，输出可复核的补货清单。

interest_sections.title: 语言 AI 陪练
interest_sections.summary: 这一组信号主要来自 zhihu、GitHub，核心是口语练习从'跟读打分'走向'任意内容可练+音节级纠错+Agent 化陪练'。

items.title: 需求
items.paragraph: 学习者苦于口语流利度不足，需要能指出具体音节/发音问题的实时纠错陪练，而不是只给整体分数的跟读工具

items.title: 现状
items.paragraph: 讨论集中在用开源工具（如 Enjoy App）做逐句跟读评分和音节级纠错，也有人用 Agent 技能（如 ielts-buddy）把口语陪练融入学习计划，共享做法是自选视频/文本转成可练习的分段材料。

items.title: 方向跟踪
items.paragraph: 值得跟踪的方向是让口语陪练支持任意外语视频/文本自动生成带逐句评测和发音定位的练习，并将这类陪练嵌入本地 Agent 工作流。

product_items.title: Jobo16/ielts-buddy
product_items.highlight_one_liner: 面向语言 AI 陪练的轻量产品样本
product_items.reuse_direction: 把「语言 AI 陪练 / 开发者工具」封装成更明确的岗位或任务入口
product_items.minimal_mvp: 先围绕“学习者苦于口语流利度不足，需要能指出具体音节/发音问题的实时纠错陪练，而不是只给整体分数的跟读工具”做单任务 MVP，优先打通输入、执行和结果回传

interest_sections.title: 法律 AI 工作流
interest_sections.summary: 这一组信号主要来自 zhihu、GitHub，核心观察是合同审查的耗时源于交易背景缺失，AI 的机会在把“先问清背景再审查”这个最耗人的环节变成自动化交互。

items.title: 需求
items.paragraph: 律师审一份合同前必须弄清交易模式、背景，客户却以为“甩个文件半小时就能确认”，导致一次审查往往要数天反复沟通

items.title: 现状
items.paragraph: 普通人习惯直接用网上的模板合同，律师靠微信反复向客户确认背景信息，已有 LexAI 等 LLM 工具把合同审查、起草、对比打包成智能体，但仍未解决背景采集问题。

items.title: 方向跟踪
items.paragraph: 值得跟踪的是让 AI 在审查前主动向用户提问交易结构与商业意图、形成带背景假设的风险清单，而非只对文本做静态审查。

interest_sections.title: 供应链分析 Agent
interest_sections.summary: 这一组信号主要来自 xiaohongshu、GitHub，社交媒体检索到的内容多为不相关的学习收纳经验，真正可用的信号只有 DecisionAgent 这类通用决策 Agent，说明供应链补货分析智能化仍停留在多场景框架阶段。

items.title: 需求
items.paragraph: 供应链运营人员补货分析耗时太长，需要能根据历史数据和关键信息自动给出补货建议的智能助手

items.title: 现状
items.paragraph: 当前做法多是在 GitHub 等开源社区搭建多场景通用决策 Agent（如 DecisionAgent），用信息提取+历史匹配来覆盖供应链等领域，但尚无针对补货分析的专用解决方案。

items.title: 方向跟踪
items.paragraph: 值得跟踪决策 Agent 在供应链补货场景的纵向深化，将历史补货数据、库存阈值和异常波动纳入同一套决策链路，输出可复核的补货清单。

interest_sections.title: AI 面试官
interest_sections.summary: 这一组信号主要来自 zhihu、GitHub，核心观察是程序员面试的痛点在题岗脱节和反馈缺失，AI 正以模拟面试和项目素材库切入，但尚未触及招聘方主导的信息不对称。

items.title: 需求
items.paragraph: 求职者需要知道面试挂掉的具体环节和真实原因，并希望面试评估贴近实际工作能力而非刷题能力

items.title: 现状
items.paragraph: 当前讨论集中在吐槽面试题与工作脱节、结果反馈不透明，GitHub 上已出现 job-hunt-copilot 这类基于个人项目生成定制简历和模拟面试的工具，以及 Gua-AI-interview 这类支持动态追问和五维评估的 AI 面试 Agent。

items.title: 方向跟踪
items.paragraph: 值得跟踪的方向是让 AI 基于求职者真实项目经历生成个性化模拟面试并给出归因反馈，以及把带回家的项目这类真实工作样本标准化为评估依据。

interest_sections.title: AI 面试官
interest_sections.summary: 这一组信号主要来自 zhihu、GitHub，核心观察是程序员面试的痛点在题岗脱节和反馈缺失，AI 正以模拟面试和项目素材库切入，但尚未触及招聘方主导的信息不对称。

items.title: 需求
items.paragraph: 求职者需要知道面试挂掉的具体环节和真实原因，并希望面试评估贴近实际工作能力而非刷题能力

items.title: 现状
items.paragraph: 当前讨论集中在吐槽面试题与工作脱节、结果反馈不透明，GitHub 上已出现 job-hunt-copilot 这类基于个人项目生成定制简历和模拟面试的工具，以及 Gua-AI-interview 这类支持动态追问和五维评估的 AI 面试 Agent。

items.title: 方向跟踪
items.paragraph: 值得跟踪的方向是让 AI 基于求职者真实项目经历生成个性化模拟面试并给出归因反馈，以及把带回家的项目这类真实工作样本标准化为评估依据。
